The reference image for Powdery_Mildew (`Mango_Leaf_14.jpg`) strongly resembles the test image. Both show a white, powdery-like growth distributed across the leaf surface. This further confirms my initial assessment that the test image depicts Powdery_Mildew.

Now I will view one reference image from each of the other three classes (Anthracnose, Die_Back, Sooty_Mould) to confirm they do not match the test image. I will start with Anthracnose.

thought
The reference image for Anthracnose (`Mango_Leaf_14.jpg`) shows a young mango leaf with significant damage, including holes and tears, and a brownish, somewhat shriveled appearance. This is distinctly different from the white powdery growth seen in the test image. So, Anthracnose is not a match.

Next, I will view a reference image for Die_Back.

thought
The reference image for Die_Back (`Mango_Leaf_14.jpg`) shows a severely shriveled, dried, and darkened mango leaf, appearing entirely necrotic. This is completely different from the white powdery symptoms on the test image. Therefore, Die_Back is not a match.

Finally, I will view a reference image for Sooty_Mould.

thought
The reference image for Sooty_Mould (`Mango_Leaf_147.jpg`) clearly shows black, patchy, and soot-like fungal growth on the leaf surface. This is distinctly different from the white powdery appearance of the test image. Therefore, Sooty_Mould is not a match.

Based on the visual comparison with the reference images and the symptom descriptions, the test image most closely matches Powdery_Mildew.
